title: Never run image and video ads together
description: Never run image and video ads together
transcript: The ad platforms treat images and videos very differently. Right. For example, Facebook will almost always prioritize images over videos, and Instagram will almost always prioritize, uh, videos over images. Or at least that's been my experience so far. So it's really important that you are creating, um, multiple different campaigns, one for videos and one for images. And you're gonna see that happen a lot of times as we're talking about this, even when we get to the scaling campaigns as well. And the other reason I really like images versus videos is because, once again, you. A lot of. You think, oh, uh, the biggest issue that I have is I. I'm, uh, not able to get a winning ad campaign. But the biggest issue is how do I spend more on that winning ad campaign? And the more testing that you can do and the more winning ad creatives that you have, the more ad spend you'll be able to put behind it. And so by separating out between videos and images, it's not like you're trying to allocate the same ad spend between an image or a video. You're gonna be able to essentially duplicate the ad spend. Let's say $2,000 a day going to your winning videos and $2,000 a day going to your winning images, which means you can spend $4,000 a day.
